additionalCoursework:
English (6 credit hours)
Other Humanities and Behavioral Sciences (12 credit hours)

AP credit is accepted for the English and Other Humanities and Behavioral Sciences requirements.

Humanities-based writing-intensive coursework may be used as a substitute for the English requirement. Humanities is a broad category, including fine arts, history, philosophy, etc. Business, health or science-based courses cannot be used to fulfill the humanities or English requirements. 

Applicants must have at least 18 credit hours total of English and/or humanities courses, and one course cannot satisfy two requirements. Please include a course description with the secondary application when using a writing-intensive substitution.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
In keeping with our Ignatian Mission, the School of Medicine will be a place where everyone is welcomed, respected, and supported, so that we may be a community-responsive leader, working in partnership to reduce health inequities and improve the health and well-being of the St Louis region. The Saint Louis University School of Medicine is committed to the education of a culturally competent healthcare workforce.  We seek to immerse SLU's medical students and graduate medical residents in a training atmosphere that prepares them for the practice of medicine within the communities we serve.

Our focus includes:
- Strengthen recruitment/retention efforts
- Development and promotion of internal talent
- Create and support mentoring programs
- Offer education and training opportunities
- Increase collaboration between Saint Louis University School of Medicine and the St. Louis community
- Fostering the Jesuit tradition - agents of change who work to bring about a more just, humane world
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A Leave of Absence is available to students in good academic standing for personal or medical reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: All specialties have associated interest groups. We provide longitudinal electives, quality time and emphasize wellness.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The medical school is located in the city's arts district, five minutes from the Gateway Arch on the Mississippi Riverfront. Recent neighborhood developments have created new opportunities for housing, shopping, dining and recreation.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: St. Louis and the surrounding area offer abundant affordable housing compared to the national average.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: In keeping with our Jesuit mission, we’re constantly striving to foster an environment that welcomes all expressions. Learn more at https://www.slu.edu/cross-cultural-center-for-global-citizenship/lgbtqia-support/index.php and https://www.slu.edu/diversity/index.php
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Office of Student Affairs has several resources available to support students. In addition to our Office of Learning Services that is open and available to all students, the Office of Student Affairs assists students navigating accommodations for the curriculum around testing and other adjustments to the learning environment in the settings of disabilities. We also work in conjunction with Saint Louis University Center for Accessibility and Disability Resources for additional support.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Saint Louis University is concerned about the well-being and success of our medical students and trainees. The Behavioral Health Program provides medical school students and SLU GME trainees access to confidential, professional behavioral health services at no out-of-pocket cost. Under the Behavioral Health Program, students and trainees can receive consultation for any problem or life event that may be causing distress or to enhance personal wellness.

The Office of Student Affairs provides guidance, support and administrative assistance to all of our medical students. The office's staff maintains an open-door policy, and is available to answer questions and offer support. The office coordinates important events like the first-year orientation, the annual White Coat Ceremony and various commencement activities. The office also acts as a liaison to faculty and administration, and assists with academic advising and personal counseling.

Other areas of responsibility of the office include, but are not limited to:

Overseeing career advising services for students in all years
Overseeing student-run organizations
Supervising the election of class officers
Advising students on research opportunities
Participating in the writing of medical student performance evaluations/dean's letters
Guiding students interested in rotations/electives in foreign countries
Scheduling town hall meetings with the dean, the dean's staff and interested students

The Simon Recreation Center — in the heart of the undergrad campus — offers drop-in recreational opportunities, as well as scheduled programs and events. It’s 120,000 square feet of activity, featuring six indoor basketball courts, four racquetball/handball courts, a bouldering wall, fitness center, spinning studio and indoor pool. Additional facilities, both indoor and outdoor, are available throughout our campus.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: SLU SOM fosters a collaborative environment among students and faculty in a way that few medical schools do. Student feedback and input is fundamental to all major changes at SLU SOM. The student voice is prominent and a tremendous engine for change. We emphasize making the complete physician who is outstanding at both the science and art of medicine. We emphasize cura personalis, which is care for the entire person. Included in care for the entire person is care for oneself. Wellness and approaches to handling the challenges of the healthcare field are a priority and emphasized throughout the curriculum. Wellness programming occurs throughout the academic year and is threaded through the curriculum. Additionally, our new student wellness and lounge space was completely remodeled with the support of alumni and the Dean’s office. In the 2024 academic year, we have added a remodeled gym space for student use on campus.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students are required to have a vehicle by the time they reach clinical rotations

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional dress and white coats are expected when dealing with patients/standardized patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Arranged as needed and readily available.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students can begin interacting with patients as early as Year 1 through courses and electives.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture, Lab, Active Learning (peer instruction, team-based learning, simulation, small group), Online Courses
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students see a variety of patient types and conditions to ensure appropriate coverage of the most common and serious conditions across the seven required core clerkships and during their fourth year.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are ranked by quartile based on core clerkship grades. The student quartile is included in the medical student performance evaluation (MSPE) that goes to residency programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Active learning sessions are required. A few lectures are required. Otherwise, lecture attendance is not required.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The MD curriculum provides integration of basic, clinical, and health systems sciences across all four years. Our pre-clerkship experience uses an active learning-based curriculum rooted in instructional methods that includes team-based learning, peer instruction, simulation, and other small-group active learning. The content is delivered over 18 months through organ-based module systems, where students learn about the normal human body before moving to abnormal pathology. Prior to entering the clerkship curriculum in January of Year 2, fundamental clinical skills are achieved through Clinical Interviewing and Clinical Diagnosis courses. Core clinical clerkships are completed at numerous sites in the St. Louis area, honing clinical skills with a patient focus that emphasizes cura personalis, care for the whole person. In January of year 3 through graduation, students take clinical electives that prepare them for their future specialty (including away rotations), an acting internship, and an internship preparation capstone course.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Interdisciplinary education and a Medical Home
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Distinction in Research Award. Summer research opportunities and stipends are available between 1st and 2nd year. There are numerous research opportunities in both basic science and clinical departments.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: All students participate in service activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Major teaching affiliations include SSM Saint Louis University Hospital, SSM Cardinal Glennon Children's Hospital, SSM St. Mary's Hospital, VA St. Louis Health Care System-John Cochran Division.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Grading is pass/fail for the pre-clerkship (or first three semesters) and honors, near-honors, pass/fail for the clinical years.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The School of Medicine offers students a comprehensive education that incorporates disease prevention and treatment with compassionate care delivered in a team setting. Importantly, our students and trainees are also involved in scientific studies so they are trained in the latest disease management techniques.

Our four-year M.D. program integrates the basic and clinical sciences through an organ system approach to medical education. Didactic settings are varied and include small group activities, computer-based instruction and case-based tutorials.

Our Clinical Skills Center offers students the opportunity to interact with trained standardized patients and practice selected clinical procedures on simulated models and mannequins before participating in the care of actual patients.

During third- and fourth-year clinical rotations, students continue developing their diagnostic and treatment competencies in a variety of supervised inpatient and outpatient settings.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission and Values
The mission of the Saint Louis University School of Medicine is the pursuit of excellence in education, research, clinical care and community engagement through professional development, collaboration and social justice.

Core Values: 
Cura Personalis – Care for the whole person, rooted in the Ignatian principle that God created us to do good in the world, and embracing the humanity in all
Scholarship – Delivering transformative education and creating new knowledge
Discovery – Research, scientific inquiry, and the application of that knowledge
Equity – Striving for justice, fairness, and diversity in our education, research and service to the community
Collaboration – Partnership across Saint Louis University, SSM Health and the wider community 

Established in 1836, the school has the distinction of awarding the first medical degree west of the Mississippi River and proud to be part of the 450-year tradition of Jesuit education.

The School of Medicine trains physicians and scientists, conducts medical research, and provides health services on a local, national and international level. We strive to graduate physicians who manifest in their personal and professional lives an appreciation for humanistic medicine. Grounded in Jesuit values, we serve our community, which faces challenges of poor health indicators, education, poverty and racism and the School of Medicine continues to work for health equity and well-being of our neighbors. 

We embody Cura Personalis (“care for the individual person”). Our work goes beyond training physicians to be scholars of the human body. We graduate doctors who appreciate humanistic medicine, concern themselves with the sanctity of human life and commit to dignity and respect for all patients.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: It is the responsibility of the applicant to assure that all of the necessary documents reach the Committee on Admissions. Please remember that your application is not complete until all letters of recommendation have been received. Please do not send additional letters of recommendation, only the 3 required letters.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letters of recommendation in support of your application are required for a complete application. If your school has a pre-medical advisory committee, a letter from the committee is sufficient, and you also have the option to supplement your committee letter with two additional letters of your choosing. If your school does not have a committee, please request three letters of recommendation. At least one of these letters should be from a college or university science professor. The two additional letters are your choice and may be from an individual that you worked with (research mentor, shadowed physician, service organizer, etc.) who may also speak to your strengths. While not required, the Admissions Committee greatly appreciates seeing a letter from a clinical or service experience that was longitudinal and meaningful to you. An insightful and in-depth evaluation by someone who knows you is of greater value than a recapitulation of your academic work.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Saint Louis University School of Medicine encourages applications from students who have achieved a high level of academic performance and who manifest in their personal lives qualities compatible with a career that serves society.

The University's mission statement affirms the value of a diverse educational environment to prepare students for life and work in a global society. To foster this mission, the School of Medicine strives to recruit, admit, retain and graduate a student body that reflects the surrounding community. 

The Committee on Admissions usually recognizes undergraduate credit given for advanced placement courses when it is indicated on a transcript. AP coursework is acceptable for pre-requisites except for required Biology and Chemistry courses. Upper-level coursework may also be used to fulfill the course requirements. 

Regarding community college coursework, the Committee prefers (a) no more than 50% of undergraduate science coursework completed and/or (b) no post-baccalaureate redemptive work completed in this manner.

PREview exam-Our Committee requires the PREview exam, but has not set an expiration date. All previous administrations will be considered for the current application cycle.

**Response to COVID-19**
As we worked through the COVID-19 pandemic, many universities modified their grading systems. We will give full consideration to pass/fail grades for any lecture or laboratory courses taken during the Spring 2020 semester. As in the past, prerequisite courses must be completed in a degree-granting university. Each course director is to determine the balance between online and classroom instruction. Rest assured, our Committee conducts a holistic review of each applicant; that semester is just one component of your entire application.

Withdrawals should be submitted by email to slumd@health.slu.edu, not via document upload.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Technical standards for the admission, retention, and graduation of applicants or medical students: This policy represents a statement by the medical school of the: 1) essential academic and non-academic abilities, attributes, and characteristics in the areas of intellectual-conceptual, integrative, and quantitative abilities; 2) observational skills; 3) physical abilities; 4) motor functioning; 5) emotional stability; 6) behavioral and social skills; and 7) ethics and professionalism that a medical school applicant or enrolled medical student must possess or be able to acquire, with or without reasonable accommodation, in order to be admitted to, be retained in, and graduate from that school’s medical educational program.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Student Financial Services Website: https://www.slu.edu/medicine/about/student-resources/financial-aid/

The mission of the Office of Student Financial Services within the Saint Louis University School of Medicine is to assist our students in identifying and providing resources to meet the costs associated with medical school. We assist in identifying and providing resources to meet the costs associated with our standard student budget.

If you need loans to meet your financial needs while attending the Saint Louis University School of Medicine, it is important to thoroughly research your options to find the best package to fit your needs. 

Eligible accepted applicants have the opportunity to apply for the University Scholarships. Scholarships are renewable pending satisfactory academic progress up to four years.  Three specific aid opportunities are listed below, but other scholarships also exist. 

- The  Spirit of St. Louis Scholarship –  Intended to promote and support highly talented students from St. Louis and the surrounding areas to attend SLU SOM. 
  
- The 1836 Scholarship – Intended to promote highly talented individuals who excel academically, in leadership or in service, who have a demonstrated financial need.

The Office of Ignatian Mission in Medicine is excited to offer a limited number of full tuition (including fees), *renewable term scholarships. 

- SLU School of Medicine Opportunity Scholarship:  The Opportunity Scholarship is intended to promote and support talented students to attend SLU SOM. 

- SLU School of Medicine Lo Family Scholarship: The Lo Family Scholarship is  intended to promote and support a talented student who is from St. Louis or the surrounding area and has been admitted to the School of Medicine.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Master of Science in Medical Science-Rigorous course study aimed at improving the strength of graduates' application to medical school or other health professional schools. Students take courses with first-year medical students. Experience hands-on training in gross anatomy, embryology, systems neurobiology and systems physiology. Opportunities available in either service, research, or clinical shadowing opportunities that fit the student's interests and needs.

Guaranteed Interview Pathway for Admission:
Offered to students who meet certain metrics and submit an application to the School of Medicine. Present criteria for a guaranteed interview include:

- Maintain a GPA of 3.25 or above per semester in the M.S.M.S. program
- MCAT score of 498 or greater
- Demonstrate clinical, service, and research activities prior to participation in the M.S.M.S. program
- Participate in at least 20 hours of local community service during the M.S.M.S. program
Upholds standards of professionalism

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The  waitlist is a ranked list. The ranking of this list is kept confidential by the Committee on Admissions. Applicants on the waitlist may be offered an acceptance at any time.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
General Biology or Zoology 8 hours*
General Chemistry 8 hours*
Organic Chemistry 8 hours*
Physics 8 hours*
English 6 hours
Other Humanities and Behavioral Sciences 12 hours
*A laboratory course is required in these sciences.

Biochemistry may be taken in place of one semester of Organic Chemistry.

AP coursework is acceptable for pre-requisites *except* for required Biology and Chemistry courses. Upper-level coursework may also be used to fulfill the course requirements.

The Committee will consider Humanities based writing-intensive coursework as a substitute for the English requirement. Humanities is a broad category, including Fine Arts, History, Philosophy, etc. Business, health or science-based courses can not be used to fulfill the Humanities or English requirement. Applicants must have at least 18 credit hours total of English and/or Humanities courses and one course cannot satisfy two requirements. 

See "Admission Policies" section for community college preferences.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Saint Louis University School of Medicine holistically evaluates all applicants who have satisfied our minimum requirements with our mission in mind. The Committee considers an applicant's path to medicine by reviewing their personal statement, science coursework, GPA progressions and MCAT scores in addition to evaluating the quality of their experiences and personal characteristics. The Committee uses a rolling admissions process and encourages submission of all materials as early in the cycle as possible.
